objective: Prove, for three rings in a chain (A and B joined by contact c1, B and C by contact c2), with binding of two rings at a contact read as every minimally decisive set of the contact's future meeting both rings' own first-row cells: (1) with listening contacts, which read their rings and feed nothing back, c2's future never depends on ring A, so the chain never binds its ends: composition across time needs a contact that the middle ring reads; (2) with shared contacts, c2(T) does not depend on ring A's first row for T <= d, d the distance between the two contacts along ring B, so the ends can be bound only from lag d + 1; (3) for linear or affine rings and affine contacts, a contact binds two rings at lag T exactly when the support of its row of M^T meets both. Check exhaustively on small chains.
status: Proved 2026-11-08: listening contacts never compose (the far contact never depends on the far ring); in a shared chain the far ring reaches the far contact only from lag d + 1, d the contacts' distance on the middle ring (reached at d + 1 in 694 of 792 configurations); affine chains bind exactly along the support of the contact's row of M^T.
title: What a chain of contacts can carry
